summary: A worktree is a second folder connected to the same repository, with a different branch checked out. You can work on two branches at once without stashing.
notes: All worktrees share one history, so the hotfix commit is visible from project right away.
A branch can be checked out in only one worktree at a time.
Next, merge hotfix into main the usual way, or push it and open a pull request.
pitfall: Deleting the worktree folder with rm -r leaves Git thinking it still exists, and the branch stays locked. Use git worktree remove, or git worktree prune after an rm.
setup_note: Starts on the branch letter-grades with one commit and an unfinished, uncommitted change to gradebook.py. README.md on main has a typo.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz socres for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"

printf '%s' 'def letter(score):
    return "A" if score >= 90 else "B"
' >> gradebook.py
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add letter grade function"
